title: TTFT regression across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — scheduler & KV-prefetch mitigation
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Summary: Starting 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC we observed a sustained increase in TTFT (median +220ms) and a tokens/sec drop (~18%) across a subset of customers routing to mixed deployment topologies (hosted -> dedicated -> private fallbacks). Impact surfaced in both short prompt and multi-turn chat flows on models rwd-base-v2 and rwd-chat-v1. Immediate customer escalations from two enterprise customers (finance and healthcare) requesting mitigation.

Suspected cause: A recent runtime kernel-selection heuristic (merged in runtime-1.20) interacts poorly with the new concurrent KV-prefetch circuit under high multiplexing, creating priority inversion and scheduler skew on certain affinity groups. Under concurrent warmup, kernels chosen cause longer single-request execution times and prefetch locks increase queueing, amplifying first-token latency and reducing sustained tokens/sec.

Goal: Deliver a safe emergency mitigation to restore SLAs and tokens/sec, capture reproducible signal, and plan a robust fix (kernel-selection refactor + prefetch guardrails).
steps_taken: 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC: Pager-on-call (Liam) ran live query of router traces and confirmed elevated first-byte latencies tied to nodes with kernel-selector version v1.20.0-rc3
2026-03-09 23:05 UTC: Rolled canary patch to disable new kernel heuristic on 10% of capacity for affected cluster (canary showed normalized TTFT within 5 minutes)
2026-03-10 01:10 UTC: Applied emergency rollback of kernel heuristic to all affected nodes (runtime-1.20 -> runtime-1.19.8 behavior) as hotfix; immediate median TTFT recovered by ~180ms
2026-03-10 03:00 UTC: Tuned KV-prefetch circuit breaker thresholds to limit inflight prefetches per-gpu, reducing lock contention under mixed tenancy
2026-03-10 05:20 UTC: Enabled temporary priority-shedder policy for bulk/low-priority routes to protect short interactive sessions

2026-03-11 10:00 UTC: Collected targeted telemetry (per-request kernel choice, prefetch queue depth, lock wait times) and replayed a 10k request synthetic workload to reproduce regression and validate hotfix effectiveness
2026-03-11 18:40 UTC: Notified impacted customers with status update and mitigation steps (see links)
acceptance_criteria: Median TTFT for affected customers returns to within 10% of baseline across hosted/dedicated/private within 24 hours of mitigation
Tokens/sec for sustained workloads recovers to baseline +/- 5% in post-hotfix synthetic replays
No regression introduced in unrelated models or regions after rollback (verified by smoke tests)
Postmortem identifies root cause with PR for long-term fix and schedule for rollout to runtime-1.21
